$comment: Shared-patch baseline (U-L3-01). Read by script/check-shared-patches.ts and script/check-opencode-annotations.ts. Each shared upstream file that Kilo adds or changes needs an entry: rung (3 = seam patch, 4 = feature patch) and the missing seam. `unmarked` allows lines without markers and states why. Raise a limit only in the PR that adds the patch, and lower it when a patch goes away.

.github/actions/setup-bun/action.yml.seam: Windows CI setup: exclude the workspace, temp and Bun directories from Defender real-time scanning before the install. Carried over from v1 (`main`). The Windows Bun cache skip that Kilo also carried is upstream since v2.0.31 (anomalyco/opencode#55866). No seam: the composite action has no input to run a step before the install, and every job that installs dependencies uses it.

.github/workflows/check.yml.seam: CI triggers and gates: run `check` on push to Kilo's `v2` integration branch (upstream's v2 line is `dev`) and for every pull request, so stacked v2 PRs that target another PR branch are checked; skip `lint:changed` on upstream sync PRs (branch `sync-v*`), whose changed files are upstream's and fail upstream's lint too. No seam: workflow triggers and step conditions cannot be extended from outside the file.

.github/workflows/test.yml.seam: CI triggers: run the unit and e2e matrix on push to Kilo's `v2` integration branch (upstream's v2 line is `dev`). Skip the `affected` job, and with it the `e2e-suite` jobs that need it and the `e2e` result check that requires `affected` to succeed: they test only `packages/app` and `packages/session-ui`, which Kilo removed (`skipFiles` in script/upstream/utils/config.ts). Job-level lines, so upstream changes to the e2e steps still merge cleanly. `Build workspace libraries` in upstream's `build` job filters only on `@opencode/cli^...`, because turbo fails on the `@opencode/app^...` filter when the package does not exist. CI speed: `Verify packed workerd SDK` runs in its own `sdk` job (at the end of the file), so it no longer waits for the unit tests in `unit`. The Turbo cache step (upstream removed its broken one in v2.0.31) uses `.turbo/cache` (where Turborepo 2.x writes), keys on turbo.json and bun.lock, and carries the shard. Test shards: a `shard` matrix dimension in `unit` (2 Linux, 3 Windows) sets `KILO_TEST_SHARD` and `KILO_TEST_CONCURRENCY`; core, tui and cli run `test:ci` (the Kilo runner, script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts), the other packages run `test` once, in shard 1; failing cases from the runner's JUnit reports become annotations, and the reports are an artifact that refreshes the shard weights. No seam: workflow triggers, job conditions, jobs, steps, matrix dimensions and cache keys cannot be extended from outside the file. Upstream has no cache key input or test shard option.

.gitignore.seam: Ignore the v1 line's local dev profile (`.kilo-dev/`, left behind when one checkout switches between `main` and `v2`), `telemetry-id`, generated dependency installs, merge reports, and JetBrains state under `.kilo/`, and `packages/app/.artifacts/`. No seam: root gitignore rules cannot live in a Kilo-owned file. The v2 `bun dev` profile moved into the Kilo host package (packages/kilo-cli/.gitignore, U-E0-01); the remaining patterns are not host entries and stay. Reconciled by 3-way merge during upstream syncs.
.gitignore.unmarked: Eleven ignore patterns. A gitignore pattern line cannot carry an inline comment, so each pattern is preceded by a `# kilocode_change:` comment line.

AGENTS.md.seam: One marked block at the top with the Kilo rules for the v2 line (integration branch `origin/v2`, moving base, branch names, `bun dev` isolation instead of `dev:live`, plugin-first placement, direction of code movement, checks), pointing at migration-context.md, the plan, the fork conventions and the skills. It overrides the upstream rules it contradicts (default branch `dev`, `dev:live` against the installed service). Instructions only, no behavior. No seam: `AGENTS.md` is the only root instruction file that every agent used on this repository reads (v2 core loads only `AGENTS.md`, `core/src/config/plugin/instruction.ts`). A Kilo `instructions` entry in a root `kilo.json` would reach Kilo sessions only, and the contradicting upstream rules would still be in this file, so the override sits next to them. The upstream text below the block stays untouched, so syncs conflict only when upstream edits the first lines.

README.md.seam: Show the generated Kilo v2 migration progress map (badge, treemap, history from migration-tracking/progress/) on the branch front page. Visibility only, no behavior. No seam: the repository README is a single upstream-owned file, and a Kilo-owned README cannot be the front page of the same repository. The Kilo host (U-E0-01) is a package and does not change the front page. Goes away when the map is published outside the repository (for example GitHub Pages).

package.json.seam: Root `dev` script runs script/dev-isolated.ts, which starts the Kilo host entry (packages/kilo-cli) with an isolated profile, so `bun dev` never uses the installed OpenCode or Kilo data. Stays after U-E0-01: `bun dev` from the root reads the upstream root package.json, and upstream's script runs the upstream CLI with the real data. Root `lint` script runs only `oxlint`: its ast-grep and `script/sdk-docs.ts` steps check `packages/gui-extensions`, which Kilo removed (`skipFiles`).

packages/cli/package.json.seam: Export `./*` (`./src/*.ts`) as `core`, `server` and `util` do, so the Kilo host (packages/kilo-cli, U-E0-01) can run the upstream command handlers and services. Generic: any embedding entry can use it. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the CLI exported only `./run` and `./server-process`, so no entry outside the package could reach `Commands`, `Runtime` or a handler. Add a `test:ci` script that runs the Kilo test runner (script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts) in balanced shards for CI. Turborepo runs only package.json scripts, so the sharded task needs a script in each sharded package (core, tui, cli); the package's own `test` script stays as it is and the runner calls it with file arguments.

packages/cli/script/app-assets.ts.seam: Build an empty web UI archive when `packages/app` does not exist, because Kilo removed it (`skipFiles` in script/upstream/utils/config.ts). One generic condition covers the release build (`build.ts`) and the Node build (`build-node.ts`). The server then answers non-API paths with 404, as on v1. No seam: the build scripts call `buildAppArchive` directly.

packages/cli/script/service-smoke.ts.seam: Accept a 404 for the web UI shell in the compiled service smoke test, because the Kilo build embeds no web UI (`packages/app` removed). The API, authentication, and plugin checks still run. No seam: the smoke script has no option to skip the web UI check.

packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/mcp/a.seam: Kilo config discovery: read `kilo.json`, `kilo.jsonc`, `.kilo` and `.kilocode` in Kilo v1 order (directory candidates before root files, `.kilocode` before `.kilo`), and keep writing `kilo.json`. Upstream discovery has fixed names and order and no plugin or host seam can change it, so the shared discovery file carries the difference. Test files mirror the same behavior.

packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/plugi.seam: Kilo config path for plugin commands: resolve `kilo.json`, `kilo.jsonc`, `.kilo` and `.kilocode`, and only root files in the global directory, like Kilo v1. Shared CLI handlers with no plugin seam for config path selection.

Kilo config path for plugin commands: resolve `kilo.json`, `kilo.jsonc`, `.kilo` and `.kilocode`, and only root files in the global directory, like Kilo v1. Shared CLI handlers with no plugin seam for config path selection.

packages/cli/src/server-process.ts.seam: `Options.overrides` (service replacements), passed through to `ServerProcess.start` in packages/server/src/process.ts, so an embedding entry's `serve` handler can replace services in the server it starts. The Kilo host registers the Kilo plugins this way (`SdkPlugins.node` replacement, U-E0-01). Two lines, no Kilo value. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: `run` built the server options itself and had no way to add a replacement.

packages/core/package.json.seam: Add a `test:ci` script that runs the Kilo test runner (script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts) in balanced shards for CI. Turborepo runs only package.json scripts, so the sharded task needs a script in each sharded package (core, tui, cli); the package's own `test` script stays as it is and the runner calls it with file arguments.

packages/core/src/config.ts.seam: Kilo config discovery: read `kilo.json`, `kilo.jsonc`, `.kilo` and `.kilocode` in Kilo v1 order (directory candidates before root files, `.kilocode` before `.kilo`), and keep writing `kilo.json`. Upstream discovery has fixed names and order and no plugin or host seam can change it, so the shared discovery file carries the difference. Test files mirror the same behavior.

packages/core/src/config/discovery.ts.seam: Kilo config discovery: read `kilo.json`, `kilo.jsonc`, `.kilo` and `.kilocode` in Kilo v1 order (directory candidates before root files, `.kilocode` before `.kilo`), and keep writing `kilo.json`. Upstream discovery has fixed names and order and no plugin or host seam can change it, so the shared discovery file carries the difference. Test files mirror the same behavior.

packages/core/src/plugin/sdk.ts.seam: Registration phase for embedder plugins: `register(plugin, { phase: "post" })` and `all(phase)`. Without a phase, `all()` returns what it returned before. The Kilo agents use it: the agent ceiling must run after `ConfigAgentPlugin`, which is an internal post plugin (U-E2-12). Six lines, no Kilo value. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the store had no phase, so every embedder plugin ran before the internal post plugins and a plugin could not act on the result of config.

packages/core/src/plugin/supervisor.ts.seam: Appends the embedder plugins registered with phase `post` (`SdkPlugins.all("post")`) after the internal post plugins, so they see the result of config. One line, no Kilo value. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the supervisor builds the boot order itself and put every embedder plugin in the pre phase.

packages/core/test/config/command-subage.seam: Tests for the Kilo config discovery seam: `kilo.json`, `kilo.jsonc`, `.kilo` and `.kilocode` names and v1 order. Shared test files, marked for the same reason as the discovery seam.

packages/server/src/process.ts.seam: `ServerProcess.start` takes `overrides` (service replacements) and passes them to `createRoutes`, which already takes them (as `ServerFetch.BootOptions.overrides` does for the embedded server). Three lines, no Kilo value. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the process server built its routes without replacements, so a host could not register plugins (`SdkPlugins`) or replace services in the server the CLI spawns.

packages/tui/package.json.seam: Add a `test:ci` script that runs the Kilo test runner (script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts) in balanced shards for CI. Turborepo runs only package.json scripts, so the sharded task needs a script in each sharded package (core, tui, cli); the package's own `test` script stays as it is and the runner calls it with file arguments.

packages/tui/src/component/dialog-integr.seam: Prompt for Personal Account vs Team (`chooseKiloAccount`) after a Kilo Gateway login completes, before closing or chaining the integration dialog. `TuiPlugin` has no post-integration-connect hook.

packages/tui/src/plugin/builtins.ts.seam: Register the built-in `KiloTeams` TUI plugin (`/teams`, `/team`, `/org`, `/orgs`). Stays after U-E0-01: the TUI loads its built-in list in the TUI process, which `SdkPlugins` (a server store) does not reach. The config-driven path (`plugins` in the TUI config, loaded by `tui/src/plugin/context.tsx`) loads only npm packages or local files, which a compiled binary does not have. A generic seam needs an `@opencode/tui` export of the list (package.json) plus an extension point in this file, which is not fewer shared lines than these two.

packages/util/src/global.ts.seam: The app directory name under the XDG bases (`const app`) reads `OPENCODE_APP_DIR_NAME` and defaults to `opencode`, so an embedding entry can name its own config, data, cache, state and tmp directories. The Kilo host sets `kilo2` in packages/kilo-cli/src/env.ts before any upstream module loads (U-E1-01 part 1, D-4). One line, no Kilo value. Rung 2 cannot supply it: `Global.layerWith` replaces only the service in one graph, while `Global.Path` and `Flock.setGlobal({ state })` are computed when this module loads and read statically by the log file (util/observability/logging.ts), the server tmp (server/src/process.ts) and the TUI themes (tui/src/mini/theme.ts); `cli/src/server-process.ts` and `cli/src/commands/handlers/default.ts` compile their own `Global` node from those defaults, so the background service and the database stayed under `opencode` with host composition alone (measured: the service read its port from `~/.config/opencode` and logged to `~/.local/share/opencode/log`).

turbo.json.seam: Define `@opencode/core#test:ci`, `@opencode/tui#test:ci` and `@opencode/cli#test:ci` (a generic `test:ci` task adds a no-op node to every package): `dependsOn: ["transit"]` like upstream's generic `test`, `env: ["KILO_TEST_SHARD"]` gives each shard its own cache key, `passThroughEnv` hands the runner its concurrency and deadline, and `inputs` add the runner and its durations from script/kilocode/test/. Upstream has no sharded test task. The `transit` task and the `@kilocode/gateway-core#test` entry that Kilo carried are upstream since v2.0.32 (generic `test` on `transit`, anomalyco/opencode#55866 and anomalyco/opencode#56117).
